name: STM32F401CCU6
title: STM32F401xB/xC: 84 MHz Arm Cortex-M4 with FPU, 128 KB or 256 KB Flash, 64 KB SRAM, USB OTG FS, 1.7 V to 3.6 V
summary: A family of 32-bit microcontrollers built on an 84 MHz Arm Cortex-M4 core with single-precision FPU, DSP instructions, an MPU and a Flash accelerator that runs code with no wait states. Parts carry 128 KB or 256 KB of Flash and 64 KB of SRAM, one 12-bit 2.4 Msps ADC with up to 16 channels, two 8-stream DMA controllers, up to 11 timers, three I2C, three USARTs, up to four SPIs (two with I2S and an audio PLL), SDIO and a USB 2.0 full-speed OTG controller with its own PHY, all from a 1.7 V to 3.6 V supply. They come in UFQFPN48, WLCSP49, LQFP64, LQFP100 and UFBGA100 for –40 °C to 85 °C or 105 °C. The STM32F401CCU6 is the 256 KB part in the 7 × 7 mm UFQFPN48 with 36 I/Os, rated –40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: Arm Cortex-M4 with FPU, 84 MHz max, 105 DMIPS
128 KB (xB) or 256 KB (xC) / 64 KB; CCU6: 256 KB / 64 KB
VDD 1.7 V (internal reset off) or 1.8 V to 3.6 V; VBAT 1.65 V to 3.6 V
22.5 mA typ at 84 MHz from Flash, peripherals on (VDD = 3.3 V); 128 µA/MHz with peripherals off
Stop 42 µA typ (low-power regulator, Flash in Stop), 10 µA typ (Flash deep power-down); Standby 2.4 µA typ at 1.8 V with RTC on
12-bit, 2.4 Msps, up to 16 channels (10 on 48/49-pin parts)
HSE 4 MHz to 26 MHz, HSI 16 MHz (±1% at 25 °C), LSE 32.768 kHz, LSI 32 kHz, main PLL and audio PLL
up to 81, all 5 V tolerant; CCU6: 36
3 × I2C (1 Mbit/s), 3 × USART (10.5 Mbit/s), up to 4 × SPI (42 Mbit/s), 2 × I2S, SDIO, USB 2.0 FS OTG, SWD/JTAG with ETM
UFQFPN48 7 × 7 mm, WLCSP49 2.965 × 2.965 mm, LQFP64, LQFP100, UFBGA100

notes: STM32F401xB is the 128 KB group (CB, RB, VB) and STM32F401xC the 256 KB group (CC, RC, VC).

An order code adds the package letter, the temperature digit (6: –40 °C to 85 °C, 7: –40 °C to 105 °C) and the packing (TR tape and reel, nothing for tray or tube): STM32F401CCU6 is the 256 KB UFQFPN48 part for –40 °C to 85 °C.

circuits.description: With the internal POR/PDR off, an external VDD supervisor holds the chip in reset through PDR_ON while VDD is under 1.7 V, which lets the chip run down to VDD = 1.7 V. circuits.title: Regulator OFF
circuits.description: On the UFBGA100, BYPASS_REG tied to VDD turns the internal regulator off; the 1.2 V core supply V12 then goes into VCAP_1 and VCAP_2, each decoupled with 100 nF in place of the 2.2 µF parts. An external V12 supervisor drives PA0 low while V12 is under its minimum, acting as the power-on reset of the core domain; NRST may carry an application reset. VDD stays above VCAP_1 and VCAP_2 at all times. If V12 reaches its minimum before VDD reaches 1.7 V, PA0 is held low until both have; otherwise PA0 can be pulled low from outside. If V12 drops under its minimum while VDD is above 1.7 V, a reset is asserted on PA0. PA0 is then not a GPIO, and debug under power-on reset needs PA0 and NRST handled separately.

operation.text: Arm Cortex-M4 with single-precision FPU, MPU and DSP instructions, to 84 MHz (105 DMIPS, 1.25 DMIPS/MHz in Dhrystone 2.1), with the ART accelerator giving zero-wait execution from Flash. Up to 256 KB Flash and 64 KB SRAM. Supply from 3.6 V down to 1.8 V with the internal PDR on, or 1.7 V with it off, for core and I/Os; POR, PDR, PVD and BOR; 4 MHz to 26 MHz crystal oscillator, 16 MHz trimmed RC, 32 kHz oscillator for the RTC with calibration, 32 kHz internal RC. Run 128 µA/MHz with peripherals off; Stop 42 µA typ (65 µA max) at 25 °C with Flash in Stop and fast wakeup, down to 10 µA typ (28 µA max) with Flash in deep power-down; Standby 2.4 µA at 25 °C and 1.7 V without RTC, 12 µA at 85 °C; RTC on VBAT 1 µA at 25 °C. One 12-bit 2.4 Msps ADC with up to 16 channels; two 8-stream DMA controllers with FIFOs and bursts; up to 11 timers (six 16-bit, two 32-bit, to 84 MHz, each with up to four capture/compare/PWM channels or a pulse or quadrature encoder input; two watchdogs; SysTick). SWD and JTAG debug with the Embedded Trace Macrocell. Up to 81 I/Os, all able to interrupt and all 5 V tolerant, up to 78 of them fast to 42 MHz. Up to 11 interfaces: three I2C (1 Mbit/s, SMBus/PMBus), three USARTs (two at 10.5 Mbit/s, one at 5.25 Mbit/s; ISO 7816, LIN, IrDA, modem control), up to four SPIs (42 Mbit/s at 84 MHz), two of them with full-duplex I2S clocked from an audio PLL or an external clock, SDIO, and USB 2.0 full-speed device/host/OTG with on-chip PHY. CRC unit, 96-bit unique ID, RTC with sub-second resolution and calendar.

Six parts: CB, RB and VB with 128 KB Flash, CC, RC and VC with 256 KB, all with 64 KB SRAM. C parts come in the UFQFPN48 or WLCSP49 (36 I/Os, 10 ADC channels, no SDIO, three SPIs), R parts in the LQFP64 (50 I/Os), V parts in the LQFP100 or UFBGA100 (81 I/Os, four SPIs). All run from 1.7 V (PDR off) to 3.6 V and to 84 MHz, at –40 °C to 85 °C (suffix 6) or –40 °C to 105 °C (suffix 7) ambient. The peripherals hang off two APB buses and two AHB buses through a 32-bit multi-AHB bus matrix.

Software and features match the rest of the STM32F4 series (F405/F407, F41x, F42x, F43x), and the F401 drops into an LQFP64 or LQFP100 footprint for them with small board changes. On the LQFP64, pin 30 (PB11 on the others) becomes VCAP_1, pin 31 becomes VSS and pin 47 (VCAP2 on the others) becomes VSS, with the single VCAP capacitor raised to 4.7 µF at ESR of 1 Ω or less. On the LQFP100, PB11 is likewise replaced by VCAP_1.

The Cortex-M4 adds DSP instructions and a single-precision FPU to the Cortex-M3 instruction set and runs Cortex-M3 binaries. The ART accelerator, an instruction prefetch queue and branch cache in front of the 256-bit-wide Flash, gives CoreMark performance equal to zero-wait-state execution up to 84 MHz.

The MPU splits memory into up to 8 protected regions, each divisible into 8 subregions, from 32 bytes up to the full 4 GB. An access the MPU forbids can be caught by an RTOS, whose kernel can reprogram the regions per task. It can be left unused.

Up to 256 KB of Flash holds program and data. Up to 64 KB of system SRAM is read and written at CPU speed with no wait states. The bus matrix links the CPU and the two DMA controllers to Flash, SRAM and the AHB and APB peripherals so that several fast peripherals can work at once. Parts ship with Flash erased.
Computes a CRC over 32-bit words with a fixed polynomial, for example to check Flash contents at run time against a signature made at link time (an EN/IEC 60335-1 measure).

DMA1 and DMA2 are dual-port controllers with 8 streams each, moving data between memory and peripherals in any direction, and memory to memory, with FIFOs, bursts, circular buffers and double buffering. Each stream has hardware requests plus a software trigger, and source and destination sizes are independent. SPI/I2S, I2C, USART, the timers, SDIO and the ADC can use DMA.

The NVIC has 16 priority levels and up to 62 maskable channels besides the 16 core interrupt lines, with tail chaining, late-arrival handling and automatic state saving. The EXTI has 21 edge detectors, each set for rising, falling or both edges and masked on its own, with a pending register; it catches pulses shorter than an APB2 clock period. Up to 81 GPIOs map onto its 16 external lines.

The chip starts on the 16 MHz internal RC (1% at 25 °C). The system clock can then be the RC or a 4 MHz to 26 MHz external source, which can be monitored: on its failure the chip falls back to the RC and can raise an interrupt. Either feeds the main PLL, up to 84 MHz. The AHB buses and APB2 run to 84 MHz and APB1 to 42 MHz. APB2 timers clock up to 84 MHz and APB1 timers up to 42 MHz. A separate audio PLL (PLLI2S) lets the I2S master clock reach every standard rate from 8 kHz to 192 kHz. USB OTG FS needs a 48 MHz clock from the PLL running on the HSE.

The boot pins pick user Flash, system memory or SRAM at start-up. System memory holds the boot loader, which reprograms Flash over USART1 (PA9/PA10), USART2 (PD5/PD6), USB OTG FS in device mode (PA11/PA12, DFU), I2C1 (PB6/PB7), I2C2 (PB10/PB3), I2C3 (PA8/PB4), SPI1 (PA4 to PA7), SPI2 (PB12 to PB15) or SPI3 (PA15, PC10 to PC12); application note AN2606 describes it.

VDD runs 1.8 V to 3.6 V for the I/Os and the internal regulator, or 1.7 V to 3.6 V with the internal POR/PDR off and an external supervisor on VDD and PDR_ON. VDDA (1.7 V to 3.6 V) powers the ADC, reset blocks, RCs and PLLs and is tied to VDD, with VSSA to VSS, each pair decoupled. VBAT (1.65 V to 3.6 V) keeps the RTC, the 32 kHz oscillator and the backup registers alive through a power switch when VDD is absent. All supply and ground pins are always connected.

With PDR_ON high (and on every package without that pin), the internal POR/PDR holds the chip in reset below about 1.7 V and releases it from 1.8 V, so no external reset part is needed. After POR the option bytes load, which set one of three BOR thresholds or turn BOR off. The PVD, enabled by software, compares VDD/VDDA with a chosen threshold and interrupts on crossing it either way. With PDR_ON low (WLCSP49 and UFBGA100 only), POR/PDR, BOR and PVD are off, VBAT is not available and is tied to VDD, and an external supervisor keeps the chip in reset while VDD is under 1.7 V.

The core regulator has main mode (run, with voltage scaling to trade frequency against power: scale 3 to 60 MHz, scale 2 to 84 MHz), low-power mode (Stop) and power-down (Standby, where the core domain loses its registers and SRAM). It needs ceramic capacitors on VCAP_1 and, on the LQFP100 and UFBGA100, VCAP_2. Only the UFBGA100 can bypass it, with BYPASS_REG high: V12 is then supplied on VCAP_1/VCAP_2 at a level matched to the target frequency, the VCAP capacitors become 100 nF, there is no internal V12 monitoring, an external supervisor drives PA0 as the core-domain reset, and Standby is not available.

The backup domain holds the RTC and 20 32-bit backup registers (80 bytes), kept while VDD is off and not cleared by system reset, power reset or Standby wakeup. The RTC is a BCD calendar (seconds to year, 12/24 hour, automatic month lengths and leap years) with sub-seconds in binary, two maskable alarms, a 16-bit auto-reload wakeup timer from 120 µs to 36 hours, wakeup from Stop and Standby, and a reference-clock input (50 Hz or 60 Hz) for accuracy. It runs from a 32.768 kHz crystal, resonator or oscillator, the 32 kHz internal RC, or the HSE divided by 128; a 20-bit prescaler gives 1 s from 32.768 kHz, and a 512 Hz output allows calibration.

Sleep stops only the CPU; any interrupt or event wakes it. Stop keeps SRAM and registers but stops every clock in the 1.2 V domain and turns off the PLL, HSI and HSE, with the regulator in normal or low-power mode; any EXTI line (16 external lines, PVD, RTC alarm, wakeup, tamper or time stamp) wakes it. Standby turns the regulator off and loses SRAM and registers except the backup domain; NRST, the IWDG, a rising edge on WKUP or an RTC event wakes it. Standby is not available with the regulator bypassed. Running on VBAT, external interrupts and RTC events do not end VBAT operation.

TIM1 is a 16-bit advanced-control timer: four channels for input capture, output compare, edge- or centre-aligned PWM or one-pulse mode, complementary outputs with programmable dead time, full 0-100% modulation, and its own DMA requests. TIM2 and TIM5 (32-bit) and TIM3 and TIM4 (16-bit) are up/down counters with 16-bit prescalers and four channels each, DMA, quadrature encoder and Hall sensor inputs. TIM9 (two channels), TIM10 and TIM11 (one channel) are 16-bit up counters. All can be chained through the timer link and frozen in debug.

The independent watchdog is a 12-bit down counter with an 8-bit prescaler on the 32 kHz internal RC, so it runs in Stop and Standby; it resets the chip or serves as a timeout timer, set by hardware or software through the option bytes. The window watchdog is a 7-bit down counter on the main clock with an early-warning interrupt. SysTick is a 24-bit auto-reload down counter with a maskable interrupt at zero and a selectable clock.

Up to three I2C interfaces, master and slave, multimaster, standard (100 kHz) and fast (400 kHz) mode, up to 1 MHz on request; 7- and 10-bit addressing and dual 7-bit slave addresses, hardware CRC, SMBus 2.0/PMBus, DMA. Each has an analog spike filter (50 ns and wider) and a digital filter of 1 to 15 peripheral clocks. The SDA and SCL pins are not true open-drain: in open-drain mode their PMOS to VDD is off but present. fPCLK1 is at least 2 MHz for standard mode, 4 MHz for fast mode, and a multiple of 10 MHz for exactly 400 kHz.

USART1, USART2 and USART6 do asynchronous links, IrDA SIR, multiprocessor and single-wire half-duplex modes, and LIN master/slave. USART1 and USART6 reach 10.5 Mbit/s and USART2 5.25 Mbit/s. USART1 and USART2 add hardware RTS/CTS, smartcard (ISO 7816) and synchronous SPI-like operation. All can use DMA.

Up to four SPIs, master or slave, full duplex or simplex, 8- or 16-bit frames, eight master baud rates from a 3-bit prescaler, hardware CRC for SD/MMC, TI mode, DMA. SPI1 and SPI4 reach 42 Mbit/s and SPI2 and SPI3 21 Mbit/s. Two I2S interfaces share SPI2 and SPI3: master or slave, full duplex or simplex, 16- or 32-bit, 8 kHz to 192 kHz, with a master clock output of 256 × Fs for an external codec, clocked from PLLI2S or an external clock on I2S_CKIN; PLLI2S can change rate without disturbing the main PLL.

SD/SDIO/MMC host to 48 MHz: MMC 4.2 with 1-, 4- or 8-bit buses, SD memory 2.0, SDIO 2.0 with 1- or 4-bit buses, and CE-ATA 1.1; one SD/SDIO/MMC4.2 card at a time, or a stack of MMC4.1 or older. Not on the UFQFPN48 or WLCSP49 parts.

USB 2.0 full-speed device, host or OTG (OTG 1.0) with on-chip transceivers and no external resistors needed: 320 × 35-bit shared FIFO with dynamic sizing, SRP and HNP, 4 bidirectional endpoints and 8 host channels (periodic OUT supported), suspend and resume. Host or OTG use with a bus-powered device needs an external power switch. It works from VDD = 2.7 V, with degraded D+/D- characteristics between 2.7 V and 3.0 V.

Each GPIO is an input (floating, pull-up or pull-down), an output (push-pull or open-drain, either with a pull resistor or without), an alternate function or analog. All are high-current capable with selectable speed, can toggle up to 84 MHz, and their configuration can be locked by a register sequence. Every I/O is a floating input during and after reset unless its pin entry says otherwise.

One 12-bit ADC with up to 16 external channels, single or scan conversion, DMA, and an analog watchdog on one, several or all channels with an interrupt outside programmed limits. Conversions can be triggered by TIM1 to TIM5. With VDDA 1.7 V to 2.4 V it runs to 1.2 Msps (fADC to 18 MHz); from 2.4 V to 3.6 V to 2.4 Msps (fADC to 36 MHz). Turning it on adds 1.6 mA on VDDA. Negative injection into any analog pin spoils conversions on other channels; a Schottky diode from the pin to ground prevents it, while positive injection within limits does no harm.

The temperature sensor gives a voltage linear in temperature (2.5 mV/°C, 0.76 V at 25 °C) on ADC_IN18, usable from VDDA 1.7 V to 3.6 V. Its offset varies from part to part, so it suits measuring changes; an external sensor serves where absolute accuracy matters. Factory readings at 30 °C and 110 °C (VDDA = 3.3 V) sit in system memory. VBAT is read through an internal 50 kΩ bridge that divides it by 4.

The SWJ-DP combines JTAG and serial wire debug: SWD uses two pins (SWDIO on JTMS, SWCLK on JTCK), and a sequence on TMS switches between the two; unused JTAG pins become GPIOs. The Embedded Trace Macrocell streams compressed instruction and data trace through a few pins (TRACECLK, TRACED0 to TRACED3) to an external trace port analyzer.

Voltages are referred to VSS. Minimum and maximum values hold over temperature, supply and frequency, tested on every part at 25 °C and TAmax; values marked as from characterization, design or simulation are not production tested, and characterized limits are mean ± 3σ. Typical values are at 25 °C and VDD = 3.3 V; typical ADC accuracy covers 95% of parts (mean ± 2σ). Curves are typical and untested. Pins are measured with a 50 pF load.

Every supply pair (VDD/VSS, VDDA/VSSA and the others) has its ceramic decoupling capacitors placed as close as possible to the pins or under them on the other side of the board; leaving them out to save space or cost can make the chip misbehave. The 4.7 µF bulk capacitor goes on one VDD pin. On the UFQFPN48 the exposed pad underneath is soldered to ground, and all leads are soldered as well.

Run currents use code equivalent to CoreMark. Unless stated, all I/O pins are inputs at a fixed VDD or VSS level with no load, peripherals are off, Flash wait states suit fHCLK and VDD, voltage scale 3 is used to 60 MHz and scale 2 above, fPCLK1 = fHCLK/2, fPCLK2 = fHCLK, and a 4 MHz external clock feeds the PLL above 25 MHz. Peripheral currents are at 84 MHz, scale 2, ART on, all pins analog.

An input with its pull-up on draws current when held low (from RPU). An input at an intermediate level draws current in its Schmitt trigger; analog mode avoids it, and ADC inputs belong in analog mode. A floating input can drift to an intermediate level or toggle with noise, so unused pins go to analog mode or to a defined level by pull resistor or output mode. A switching output draws VDD × fSW × C.

A GPIO sinks or sources up to ±8 mA, or ±20 mA with relaxed VOL/VOH; PC13, PC14 and PC15 are limited to ±3 mA, 2 MHz and 30 pF. The current drawn by all I/Os plus the run current of the chip stays within ΣIVDD and ΣIVSS (160 mA each). Above 50 MHz with VDD over 2.4 V the I/O compensation cell is used.

A 4 MHz to 26 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator, characterized with the parts in the HSE table. The resonator and load capacitors sit as close to the pins as possible to limit distortion and start-up time. CL1 and CL2 are high-quality ceramics of 5 pF to 25 pF for high frequency, usually equal; the crystal's rated load is their series value plus the pin and board capacitance, roughly 10 pF. The oscillator's critical gm is at most 1 mA/V; start-up takes about 2 ms. Application note AN2867 covers crystal choice. In bypass mode OSC_IN takes an external clock of 1 MHz to 50 MHz and the oscillator is off.

A 32.768 kHz crystal or ceramic resonator with its load capacitors as close to the pins as possible. The oscillator's critical gm is at most 0.56 µA/V and it draws at most 1 µA; start-up takes about 2 s. In bypass mode OSC32_IN takes an external clock up to 1 MHz.

NRST has a CMOS input with a permanent pull-up (RPU, 40 kΩ typ). Pulses up to 100 ns are filtered out; pulses of 300 ns and longer (VDD > 2.7 V) are taken. An internal reset drives the pin low for at least 20 µs. A 0.1 µF capacitor to ground protects against stray resets, and anything driving NRST has to pull it below VIL max.

PA0, PA1 and PA2 on the LQFP100 and PDR_ON on the WLCSP49 are only moderately robust to disturbance; a series resistor of up to 1 kΩ at the chip helps on pins that run along board tracks longer than 50 mm. Firmware should recover from a corrupted program counter, unexpected resets and corrupted control registers; holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for one second reproduces most such faults for testing (application note AN1015).
With VBUS sensing enabled, PA9 stays a floating input (its default), not an alternate function, and the sensing block draws about 200 µA through it.

Decouple VDDA and VREF+ with 1 µF in parallel with 10 nF good-quality ceramic, as close to the chip as possible: one pair where VREF+ is VDDA, two pairs where VREF+ is its own pin (VREF+ on the LQFP100; VREF+ and VREF- on the UFBGA100). Board plus pad capacitance at an analog input (about 5 pF of pad) reduces accuracy; a lower fADC compensates.

Junction temperature is TA plus PD times ΘJA, where PD is the internal power IDD × VDD plus the power in the output pins. ΘJA is 32 °C/W for the UFQFPN48, 52 °C/W for the WLCSP49, 50 °C/W for the LQFP64, 42 °C/W for the LQFP100 and 56 °C/W for the UFBGA100 (JESD51-2, still air). TJ stays within 105 °C for suffix 6 and 125 °C for suffix 7 parts.

The top side carries the product identification (for example STM32F401CCU6 on the UFQFPN48), a date code (year and week) and a revision code, oriented to the pin 1 or ball A1 identifier. Parts marked ES or E, or shipped with an engineering-sample notice, are not qualified for production.

STM32 F 401 + pin count (C 48/49, R 64, V 100) + Flash (B 128 KB, C 256 KB) + package letter (UFBGA is H, LQFP is T, UFQFPN is U, WLCSP is Y) + temperature (6: –40 °C to 85 °C, 7: –40 °C to 105 °C) + packing (TR tape and reel, none for tray or tube). STM32F401CCU6: 256 KB, UFQFPN48, –40 °C to 85 °C.
